svg.text: Everyday English - Small talk
Any plans you are looking
forward to?
MEANING
An open-ended, low-pressure question that invites someone
to share an upcoming activity.
IN CONTEXT
Any plans you are looking forward to this weekend, or are
you keeping it low-key?
USAGE NOTE
Looking forward to takes a noun or an -ing form. Keeping it
low-key means choosing something relaxed. Offer an easy
alternative so the question does not imply that exciting
plans are expected. Follow the detail your partner shares
instead of switching straight to your own story.
CONVERSATION
A: Any plans you are looking forward to this weekend?
B: A short hike, if the weather holds.
A: Nice. Have you picked a trail yet?
B: A quiet one near the lake. What about you?
A: I am keeping it low-key, probably reading at home.
B: That sounds lovely. Anything good on your reading list?
A: A mystery novel I have been saving for a quiet afternoon.
B: Enjoy it. We can compare weekend highlights on
Monday.
YOUR TURN
Respond with a plan, one detail, and a question back.
Model: I am meeting a friend for coffee near the park. Are
you doing anything outdoors?
